prompt:
You read a Twitter/X thread by Marius Hobbhahn (unrolled). Extract research choices and the reasoning he gives, as well as any views on how to do research.

Return 3-15 items. Each item is one of:
- "decision": a research decision he (or his team) made, where another choice was possible;
- "rejected": an option, method or line of work he rejected or argued against;
- "disagreement": a place where he disagrees with a default view or practice in the field;
- "advice": advice he gives about how to do research (what to work on, how to test, how to interpret results).
Prefer research methodology (evaluation design, experimental controls, what evidence to trust, which questions to pursue, how strongly to state claims) over biography, logistics or summaries of results. Only include items the text itself supports; return {"decisions": []} if there are none. For each item give:
- item_type: decision / rejected / disagreement / advice
- point: one of D1-D6 (D1 which experiment or hypothesis to pursue; D2 what evidence to collect; D3 whether to accept a result; D4 whether to continue or drop a line of work; D5 how to interpret an ambiguous result; D6 how strongly to state a claim)
- problem: the research problem or question faced, stated neutrally (1 sentence)
- did: what he chose, did or recommends (1 sentence)
- alternatives_named: a JSON list of strings, the alternatives the text itself names or rejects ([] if none)
- stated_reason: the reason the text gives ("" if none)
- quote: a VERBATIM passage of HIS OWN words, 15-60 words, copied character for character, that shows the item. Do not paraphrase, fix spelling or punctuation, merge passages, or use ellipses.
- off_topic: true if the item is not about AI, ML or research practice (e.g. energy policy, health, productivity), else false

Return only JSON: {"decisions": [{"item_type": ..., "point": ..., "problem": ..., "did": ..., "alternatives_named": [...], "stated_reason": ..., "quote": ..., "off_topic": ...}]}

 It’s time someone did for evals what @NeelNanda5 did for mechanistic interpretability.

I want to build the evals field!

1. Which evals resources would you like to see?

2. Are you interested in contributing to any of these efforts?

3. Are you interested in funding these efforts?

Details in thread and in this blog post: lesswrong.com/posts/uoAAGzn4…

 Which resources would be most helpful? I’m primarily interested in your takes.

Some suggestions include:

1. Open Problems in Evals list: A long list of open relevant problems & projects in evals.

2. More Inspect Tutorials/Examples: Specifically, examples with deep explanations, examples of complex agent setups, and more detailed examples of the components around the evals.

3. Evals playbook: A detailed guide on how to build evals with detailed examples for agentic and non-agentic evals.

4. Salient demos: I don’t even necessarily want to build scary demos, I just want normal people to be less hit-by-a-truck when they learn about LM agent capabilities in the near future.

5. More “day-to-day” evals process resources: A lot of evals expertise is latent knowledge that professional evaluators have accumulated over time.

6. An evals slack

7. Talk through the most important evals papers

8. Evals workshops and conferences

 Are you interested in contributing to any of these efforts?

1. Right now I think the following types of contributions would be helpful:

1a. People who want to contribute more detailed Inspect tutorials / Examples as described here. I think this is a great opportunity for people who are considering working full-time on evals and want to test fit / make a name for themselves.

1b. Someone who wants to help me coordinate these efforts part time or full-time. This would be a mix of playing around with evals yourself, coordinating with other actors in evals and probably a decent amount of writing.

2. I’m very interested in other contributions as well.

3. If you’re interested, fill out this form: forms.gle/C9FeShFQiiLpP8…

 Is anyone interested in funding these efforts?

1. I’d be happy to function as a regrantor. I wouldn’t take a cut myself. I imagine most grants would be between $5-15k to pay for someone building resources full-time for a few months.

2. I’m also happy to be more of a coordinator / filter and forward people to funders if a funder is willing to do fast-turnaround grants.

3. I think the total amount of funding that would be helpful to get this off the ground is $50k-100k for the next year.
